Only the very best chefs prepare fugu fish.
Because fugu never forgives mistakes.
Of course I know what there is to cook.
It is almost the exact same thing as a carp.
Excellent, then we will take the fugu from Timur right now.
You will prepare it yourself and eat it yourself.
If you stay alive, I will admit you are better.
Wait, Chef, are you going to cook it too?
And why should I have to cook it?
It is a bet, what if you do not know how yourself?

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, вы снова к нам вернулись!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, you have returned to us again!

examples.text: А мы все уже думали, вы ушли.
examples.trans: And all of us already thought you had left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подождите, шеф, а вы тоже готовить будете?
examples.trans: Wait, Chef, are you going to cook it too?

examples.text: А я тоже пришёл форму постирать.
examples.trans: I also came to wash my uniform.

examples.text: Мне тоже по санитарным нормам нельзя.
examples.trans: I am not allowed to either under sanitary rules.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will'.

examples.text: Мне через месяц надо быть в Милане.
examples.trans: In a month I need to be in Milan.

examples.text: При разделке рыбы нужно быть предельно осторожным.
examples.trans: When filleting the fish you must be extremely careful.

examples.text: Может быть, она тебе ещё и заплатила?
examples.trans: Maybe she even paid you for it too?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я зачем должен её готовить?
examples.trans: And why should I have to cook it?

examples.text: Зачем вы это сделали, Виктор Петрович?
examples.trans: Why did you do that, Viktor Petrovich?

examples.text: Зачем ты пришёл?
examples.trans: What have you come for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: А я зачем должен её готовить?
examples.trans: And why should I have to cook it?

examples.text: Я должен работать.
examples.trans: I have to work.

examples.text: Жадность должна быть умеренная.
examples.trans: Greed should be moderate.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'bet, wager' in everyday Russian.

related.gloss: to steam oneself in a bathhouse

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

examples.text: Тогда предлагаю тебе пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose a bet to you.

examples.text: Это же пари, вдруг вы сами не умеете?
examples.trans: It is a bet, what if you do not know how yourself?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это же пари, вдруг вы сами не умеете?
examples.trans: It is a bet, what if you do not know how yourself?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся?
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Вдруг пошёл дождь.
examples.trans: Suddenly it began to rain.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know how', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Это же пари, вдруг вы сами не умеете?
examples.trans: It is a bet, what if you do not know how yourself?

examples.text: Я умею плавать.
examples.trans: I can swim.

examples.text: Он не умеет считать.
examples.trans: He can't count.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agree').

examples.text: Я согласен.
examples.trans: I agree.

examples.text: Я согласен на этот спор!
examples.trans: I agree to this bet!

examples.text: Ладно, я согласна на этот план.
examples.trans: Alright, I agree to this plan.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'write', paired with 'написать'.

examples.text: Они писали мне сообщения с его телефона.
examples.trans: They were writing messages to me from his phone.

examples.text: Почему ты не пишешь?
examples.trans: Why aren't you writing?

examples.text: Я пишу письмо.
examples.trans: I'm writing a letter.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'вещание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'will, testament' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Согласен, иди пиши завещание, Огузок!
examples.trans: Agreed, go write your will, Oguzok!

examples.text: Папа испугался и пишет своё завещание!
examples.trans: Papa got scared and is writing his will!
